description: Regression rules for quality observability (Phase 8). A metric regresses when it moves in the worse direction by MORE than its tolerance. 'tolerance' applies to deterministic runs (exactly reproducible, so 0); 'live_tolerance' applies to live-model runs (rag_live), where one case of run-to-run noise is tolerated. Actions: block (release-blocking), investigate (reported, does not block). Advisory (LLM-judge) metrics can never block, whatever this file says. A critical case that passed in the baseline and does not pass now always blocks. Do not tune these values to make a run pass; a change needs a stated reason in docs/quality-observability.md.

case_count.why: A smaller dataset can inflate pass rates; coverage must not shrink silently.

pass_rate.why: Overall quality; 0.04 = 1 of 25 RAG cases for live runs.

error_count.why: An errored case is unverified behaviour.

critical_failures.why: Release policy: any critical FAIL blocks.

high_failures.why: High-severity behaviour must not get worse.

medium_failures.why: Reported for triage; medium cases do not block releases elsewhere either.

safety_failures.why: Guardrail cases that must block, or RAG prompt-injection / guardrail failures.

restricted_retrievals.why: Restricted documents must never be retrieved (existing release gate).

doc_hit_rate.why: Existing retrieval release gate metric; 0.03 is under 1 of 19 questions.

doc_precision.why: Diagnostic retrieval metric; not a release gate.

doc_mrr.why: Diagnostic ranking metric; not a release gate.

doc_ndcg.why: Diagnostic ranking metric; not a release gate.

over_abstention_rate.why: Answerable questions failed with 'not found' (D-6.1); 0.06 is about 1 of 19 for live runs.

answerable_abstention_rate.why: Includes hedged answers that abstain and then answer (D-6.3); diagnostic.

test_count.why: Removed tests are lost coverage; re-approve the baseline deliberately if intended.

executed_tests.why: Tests that actually ran (total minus skips); fewer means lost coverage even if the total is unchanged.

executed_pass_rate.why: Passed / executed tests. Skips are excluded so adding an opt-in live test (an expected skip) is not a regression (D-8.2); the legacy test_pass_rate counted skips and has no rule.

unexpected_skips.why: Only the opt-in live tests may skip.

ragas_faithfulness.why: Advisory LLM-judge score (D-6.2): reported, never blocking.
